entries.honest_summary: First genuine Arabic VGA-console screenshot produced by the RTL-VT extension. The phrase "salaam arabi" is rendered three times, right-anchored automatically by the active RTL console mode, using real Arabic bitmap glyphs rasterised from the KacstOne Bold TrueType font. KNOWN LIMITATION: letters are DISCONNECTED (isolated forms only) because no contextual shaping is performed — this is a deliberate architectural constraint (no Unicode, no bidi, no shaping, no codepoint translation in kernel); each byte maps to exactly one fixed glyph. The screenshot is authentic proof of end-to-end RTL rendering, not of Arabic typographic shaping.
what_this_release_is: Real Arabic bitmap glyphs in an 8x16 PSF2 font (not placeholders).
Automatic right-to-left anchoring on a Linux VGA text console via kernel RTL mode.
Reproducible, hash-verified artifacts published to sultanaalyami/linux@master.
what_this_release_is_not: NOT shaped Arabic (no initial/medial/final/isolated form selection).
NOT ligated (e.g. لا is not composed; it is one glyph slot, not ل+ا).
NOT Unicode-aware. The kernel path never sees codepoints; it ships raw bytes to the framebuffer.
NOT a polished terminal font — glyph strokes at 8x16 are thin and some letters are hard to distinguish at small sizes.
changes: Rewrote tools/rtl-vt/generate_psf2.py to build a valid PSF2 v0 header (magic 72b54a86, 256 glyphs, charsize=16, width=8, height=16) and render each glyph from a system TTF via Pillow (ASCII from DejaVu Sans Mono Bold, Arabic from KacstOne Bold).

Cleaned visual_runner_wsl.sh: suppresses kernel console output on tty1 (console=ttyS0 only, loglevel=0, quiet), regenerates the PSF deterministically each run, prints the decisive Arabic phrase three times in natural byte order.
Captured rtlvt-arabic-rtl-decisive.(png|ppm) showing three right-anchored Arabic lines on a clean black screen.

reproduction_steps.title: Install WSL prerequisites (one-time)
reproduction_steps.cmd: wsl -d Ubuntu-24.04 -- sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y qemu-system-x86 busybox-static python3-pil fonts-kacst fonts-kacst-one fonts-hosny-amiri fonts-sil-scheherazade fonts-dejavu-core

reproduction_steps.title: Regenerate the real-Arabic PSF2 font from the ASCII mapping and TTFs
Run the visual runner (boots the kernel in QEMU inside WSL, captures screendump)
Verify the decisive screenshot hashes
reproduction_steps.note: Exact PNG hash may drift if the runner prints a different timestamp or if the underlying TTF version differs. The decisive visual signature (three right-anchored Arabic lines at columns 70..78) is the real acceptance criterion; hashes are a best-effort reproducibility aid.

guest_runtime_sequence_inside_qemu: printf '\033[?9000h' > /dev/tty1   # enable RTL mode (rtl-vt kernel guard)

acceptance_signature.rule: A screenshot is decisive iff it contains at least one line of connected Arabic-shaped pixels starting at the right edge of the framebuffer (pixel columns 630..718 out of 720) with a clean (mostly black) background.

known_limitations: Disconnected Arabic letters (no shaping) — each byte = one isolated glyph.
No ligatures; the lam-alef combination is stored as a single precomposed glyph in one slot, not as compositional shaping.
Glyph strokes at 8x16 are thin; some letters (e.g. ba/ta/tha variants) are only distinguishable by dot position, which is 1-2 pixels and may blur depending on renderer.
Latin text will appear as Arabic glyphs because the PSF remaps 0x41..0x7A to Arabic letters; English labels must be avoided on an RTL-VT console.
CUP cursor positioning escape \033[row;colH is mirrored under RTL mode; applications must not use absolute column addressing.
next_focus: Tune glyph legibility / explore 9x16 or 16x16 variants.
Render a longer, meaningful Arabic sentence as a second proof.
Port the kernel RTL guard behind CONFIG_RTL_VT_BYPASS without editing vt.c.

entries.summary: First captured Arabic RTL screenshot with placeholder PSF; superseded by real Arabic font release.
